items.title: 71231_Sam Wooding Oral History Interview
items.q: So, anyhow, I went to Sirota, and I said, 'Listen, have you done anything about the claque?'

ctx.x: I said, "What claque?" He said, "You know, when you go to play in Spain and Italy, you're going to run on a claque, and if the director or you don't satisfy with a certain amount of money, you in trouble. The show is in trouble." And they could close the show, because they'd keep on -- everybody'd throw some dead cats up on the stage or something like that. So, anyhow, I went to Sirota, and I said, "Listen, have you done anything about the claque?" And he says, "Yes, some of them come to me and said they wanted…
down lovely. You see, I mention that because we in America knew nothing about claques.
